logline: Jim Sarbh and Ishwak Singh as Homi J. Bhabha and Vikram Sarabhai - two scientists building India's nuclear and space programmes from nothing while Nehru's republic figures out what kind of country it wants to be.

renewal.note: Two seasons confirmed complete; no Season 3 announced as of June 2026.

bollymeter.basis: Film Companion called it 'a sprawling, heartfelt achievement'; IMDb audience at 8.8 - unusually high for a biographical drama. The show won multiple National Digital Awards and collected 43 total awards. Sarbh earned an International Emmy nomination for Best Actor. Critics noted the show's refusal to canonise its subjects as the key to its authority.

pull_quotes.text: A sincere, soaring hat-tip to Nehru's mad scientists - Rocket Boys is a sprawling, heartfelt achievement.

seasons.review_body: Rocket Boys answers a question Indian biographical drama has historically fumbled: how do you make scientists compelling television without turning their work into CGI and their relationships into melodrama? Writer-director Abhay Pannu's answer is to ground everything in the friendship between Homi Bhabha and Vikram Sarabhai - two men who disagreed about almost everything except the conviction that India could think at the world's frontier. Jim Sarbh plays Bhabha as a man whose European sensibilities are permanently in tension with the country he has chosen; Ishwak Singh's Sarabhai is the gentler, more spiritually grounded counterpoint. The show's Nehru - Regina Cassandra and Saba Azad provide the female leads - is a quiet recurring presence rather than a monument. Season 1 builds to Pokhran I with enough narrative momentum that the test itself feels earned rather than inevitable. Film Companion's Suchin described it as 'the gratifying history class we all deserve' - an assessment that holds.

episode_reviews.title: Lift Off
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The premiere introduces Homi Bhabha in Cambridge - already brilliant, already restless, already shaped by a Europe that will soon explode - before the partition era deposits him in Bombay where a country is being built. Sarbh's first few scenes establish the show's register: intellectual rigour worn lightly, ambition without vanity.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Bhabha and Sarabhai's first substantive conversation - two men recognising each other across different temperaments.

critic_note.text: Jim Sarbh announces himself as one of Indian streaming's finest performers in the first twenty minutes.

episode_reviews.title: Smiling Buddha
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The season finale - IMDb's highest-rated episode of the series at 9.2 - follows the Pokhran I nuclear test and its human costs. The show resists triumphalism: the test is a success, but the episode is about what the men building the bomb understand about what they've built. Sarbh's final scene in this episode is his finest work in the series.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Bhabha processing the test results alone - scientific achievement and moral weight simultaneously present.

critic_note.text: A finale that earns genuine historical weight through the accumulated humanity of seven prior episodes.

bollymeter.basis: Film Companion noted that season 2 shifts from character to history, which is a tradeoff - the Indira Gandhi-era politics crowd out some of the intimate friendship dynamics that made season 1 exceptional. Still well-executed, still Sarbh at full stretch, but the show's heart recedes slightly as the canvas expands.

pull_quotes.text: In Rocket Boys season 2, history takes precedence over humanity - Jim Sarbh and Ishwak Singh shine regardless.

seasons.review_body: Season 2 covers the Emergency era, India's space programme milestones and the tragic deaths of both protagonists - an enormous amount of biography to compress into eight episodes. Pannu's structural choice is to prioritise the historical record over the intimate character texture of season 1, which makes the season feel more like a dramatised Wikipedia entry in its weaker moments. But Sarbh's Bhabha facing mortality is genuinely moving, and the space programme sequences have a grandeur that the show earns through two seasons of contextual groundwork. The audience held at 8.7 on IMDb - marginally below season 1 - which accurately reflects a season that is excellent without being transformative.
seasons.season_over_season: History crowds out character - structurally more ambitious, emotionally a degree cooler.
